solve: Fitted by T-2538 to J. W. Taylor's c. 1895 photograph (the image store's 1600 x 1491 px scan, the print and the grey scale under it). In the footprint frame u runs toward Prairie Avenue (west) and v runs SOUTH from the 18th Street wall. A view camera's photograph: verticals vertical, so the camera is level; its lens is shifted (the principal point stands left of the print's middle and near the foot of the house). PLAN BEARINGS, read as x on the print against the 1911 sheet 28's trace (s28fp-1801-b1, moved into the frame through the record's position): the north-west corner at the loggia's corner pier x 995 (u 20.3, v 0); the south-west corner, the front's last edge before 1811's dark stone, x 1345 (u 20.1, v 11.2); the tower's axis x 698 (u 12.0 on the sheet's bump in the 18th Street wall); the east end of the flank under the small turret x 185 (u -17.9, v 0). A level camera with a shifted lens has five unknowns and four bearings fix all but one; the fifth is the scale, and it is taken from three independent lengths that agree: the stair's nine risers of about 0.16-0.17 m bring the principal floor to about 1.45 m, the girl on the tricycle on the 18th Street walk stands about 1.1 m, and the flank's windows read about 1.2 m wide. That gives the eye 14 m west of the front and 18.7 m north of the 18th Street wall, in the intersection, f 1350 px (about 60 degrees across the print), yaw 300.5 (looking south-east). The grade lines along the flank fall within 13 px of one another from 22 m to 55 m away, which puts the horizon at y 1111 and the eye about at the lot's grade (-0.35 m, the roadway lower than the lot). RESIDUALS: the four bearings exactly; the bowed bay's middle (x 1190) lands about 60 px north of where the sheet's bulge (v 4.8-10.2) would put it, so the sheet and the photograph disagree about where along the front the bay stands, and that is open in the match record. Heights at this camera (each read at its own wall's depth, good to about +-0.5 m near the front and +-1 m on the far flank): principal floor 1.45 m, the band over the principal storey about 4.8 m, the main cornice 8.0-8.2 m; the tower's corbel table 10 m, its eaves 12.9 m, its cone's apex 18.7 m, its finial 21.4 m; the south pavilion's gable springing about 13.9 m and its apex 17.4 m; the main roof's deck about 17.2 m and its cresting 18.9 m; the east range's eaves about 8.2 m and its turret's eaves 8.0 m, apex 12.7 m, finial 15.1 m.
